answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake while it trades, like a pearl held in escrow: honest agents earn it back with interest from completed work, while a caught cheat forfeits the deposit. An attacker who tries to wander in with thousands of sock-puppet accounts must fund each one, so the cost of the attack scales linearly. A juniper-like web of trust adds a second gate: new identities start with zero reputation and gain trading limits only through attested history with established peers, so fresh fakes cannot drain value on day one.
